 Ms. Ambiya Khatun

<, Re : Can 1 of 2015 (old No. Can 4471 of 2015) This is an application for condonation of delay in
preferring the appeal.

Mr. Krishanu Banik, learned Advocate for the appellants-claimants submits that due to wrong advice by the learned lawyer conducting the case before the learned Tribunal for filing a review against the impugned order, there has been delay of 593 days in preferring the appeal.

He further submits that by the impugned order the owners of the offending vehicle have been directed to pay the compensation amount to the claimants, however, as per the settled position of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. versus Swaran Singh and Ors., reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297, in the event of breach of condition of policy of insurance in vehicle being driven by driver having no valid licence, the principle of pay and recovery is to be applied.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. versus Swaran Singh and Ors., reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of his above submissions, he prays for condonation of delay of 593 days in preferring the appeal.
Ms. Ambiya Khatun, learned Advocate for the respondent no.1-Insurance Company does not raise any objection.
As per report of the Stamp Reporter dated 28th August, 2014, there is delay of 593 days in preferring the appeal.

sentences.text: The power under Section 5 of the Limitation Act is a discretion one and has been deliberately conferred on the Court in order that judicial power and discretion in that behalf should be exercised to advance substantial justice.

When substantial justice and technical considerations are pitted against each other, cause of substantial justice deserves to be preferred for the other side cannot claim to have vested right in injustice being done because of a non-deliberate delay.

[See Collector,
Land Acquisition versus Katiji reported in (1987)2 SCC 107].
Relying on Swaran Singh's case (supra) the appellants-claimants have raised a substantial issue in this appeal that since the learned tribunal has held that there was of breach of condition of insurance policy in vehicle being driven by driver having no valid licence, the principle of pay and recovery should have been applied.

Considering the substantive isssue involved in the appeal and also keeping in mind the beneficial piece of legislation, I am inclined to condone the delay of 593 days in preferring the appeal.
Accordingly, the delay of 593 days in preferring the appeal is condoned.
The application being CAN 1 of 2015 (old No.CAN 4471 of 2015) stands disposed of.
The appeal is formally admitted and registered.

Re : FMAT 978 of 2014 This appeal is preferred against the judgment and award dated 11th of October, 2012 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, 4th Court, Burdwan,
in M.A.C. Case No. 27 of 2011 (129/2011) under Section 166 of the Motor vehicles Act,1988.

sentences.text: Let the lower court records be called for.
Department is directed to take effective steps for bringing the lower court records from the learned Tribunal within two weeks from date.

Upon receipt of the lower court records, the Office shall examine the same and if found to be complete and in order, shall serve notice of arrival of the lower court records upon the learned advocate for appellants- claimants as well as learned Advocate for the respondent no.1-Insurance Company within a period of two weeks of such arrival.

Learned Advocate for the appellants-claimants upon receipt of notice of arrival of lower court records, shall prepare and file three sets of informal paper books incorporating all relevant papers and documents including the pleadings and evidence, both oral and documentary, printed or typewritten or cyclostyled, as the case may be, out of court, within a period of four weeks from the date of service of notice of arrival of lower court record on the learned Advocate for the appellant.
The appellants-claimants are directed to deposit talabana costs together with written up notice forms for causing service of notice of appeal upon the respondent nos.2 and 3.
Since the respondent no.1-Insurance Company has already entered appearance, hence service of notice of appeal upon the said respondent is also dispensed with.
